comment:
The [earlier migration-retry finding](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12883#issuecomment-5775975530) is partly addressed at `6f4d760b`. Its broad applicability should be narrowed, not treated as fully resolved.

**Verified by source inspection:** Persistent sudo failure at the initial inspection now exits nonzero, leaving the migration pending. A working sudo with an absent drop-in remains a successful no-op. Grep read errors with status greater than 1 also leave the migration pending.

## Sudo failure at the grep step can still retire the migration

In [`migrations/1790064412.sh:29-39`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/6f4d760b5373ae6f590d97f73d4034076ed7a399/migrations/1790064412.sh#L29-L39), status 1 is treated as “no matching lines.” However, sudo also returns 1 when authentication, policy or command execution fails.

The remaining conditional path, derived from source rather than executed:

```text
Existing global drop-in: sudo test -f succeeds
  -> sudo grep itself fails with status 1, no stdout
  -> treated as an empty policy; migration exits 0
  -> runner writes completion marker
  -> later normal runs skip the migration
```

**Impact:** The global rule can remain despite the migration being recorded as completed. This requires sudo to fail after the first successful inspection, for example under command-specific permissions or changed authentication state. Normally cached credentials reduce its likelihood. It preserves the old behavior, rather than introducing a new privilege grant.

**Suggested change:** Read the privileged file separately and propagate any failed read as a nonzero migration exit. Filter successfully read content locally, where grep's no-match result cannot be confused with a failed sudo invocation.

---

**Test scope:** Source-only comparison of the follow-up, migration, runner and focused test, plus sudo exit-status documentation. No runtime reproduction, real authentication, marker creation or VM validation in this follow-up.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.
